title: Designer: choosing a look from the brief
when: The brief gives a subject and maybe a feeling (cozy, serious, playful) but no visual direction, and the designer must choose one.
prompt:
Goal: One coherent direction (palette, type, shape, density) chosen from the brief with a reason, applied consistently in the stylesheet.
Steps:
1. Pull three words of feel from the brief, or infer them from the subject and audience (a law office: calm, serious, clear).
2. Pick a palette: one neutral background, one dark text color, one accent; add a soft tint of the accent for surfaces.
3. Pick type from the system stacks: a serif heading for classic feel, a sans for modern, a rounded or heavy weight for playful.
4. Pick shape and density: radius 0 to 4 px for serious, 12 px or more for friendly; generous spacing for calm, tighter for data heavy pages.
5. Write the direction in two lines in a note with the reason tied to the brief.
6. Apply it through custom properties and check text contrast on every background.
Quality bar:
- The look matches the audience.
- One accent only.
- Text contrast passes everywhere.
Pitfalls:
- A generic gradient look for every subject.
- Several accent colors competing.
- Fonts loaded from the network.
Verify:
- [ ] Direction note exists with a reason.
- [ ] Palette is three colors plus tint.
- [ ] Type uses system stacks.
- [ ] Contrast checked.
Output: style.css (or tokens.css) built on the chosen direction and a two line note explaining it.

examples.input: site para um escritorio de contabilidade
examples.output: calm, serious, clear: navy text, off white bg, teal accent, serif headings, radius 4px
